articles.summary: New study uncovers multi-lithium ion clustering in common battery electrolytes, paving the way for improved battery performance and design Schrödinger, Inc. (Nasdaq: SDGR) today announced the publication of new research in Nature that reveals critical insights into the atomic-scale structure of lithium-ion battery (LIB) electrolytes. In a joint study with researchers from Columbia University and the New York Structural Biology Center, the team discovered new insights that challenge long-held assumptions of the fundamental chemistry of lithium-ion batteries, including multi-lithium ion complexes that may play an important role in electrolyte behavior and battery function. These new mechanistic insights into electrolyte behavior have the potential to transform battery development from empirical trial-and-error toward predictive design to high-throughput, rational, computationally-driven design for higher-capacity, faster-charging, and longer-lasting batteries.
